target: D38 -- the verifier's contract survives the pipeline, and the name registry that makes it survive
note: Three protections, and the first is the discriminating observation the issue named: the verifier's contract is safe BECAUSE the survival row fails when the pipeline's write is pointed back at the shared name. The other two are the registry itself -- a claim refused, and a write refused -- because a registry that never refuses reads exactly like one that holds. The survival row now lives in `benchmarks/heavy/` -- the commit gate reached its ceiling and this slice moved fixtures rather than raising it -- so this sweep spans both tiers and the node ids say which. Every entry was run against the real code and observed to fail the named tests. Run with: uv run python tools/mutate.py benchmarks/mutations/d38-verifier-report.json

mutations.name: the-pipeline-write-is-pointed-back-at-the-shared-name
mutations.why: the pre-D38 implementation, restored exactly: the runner writes its review report to the team contract's name, so a verifier-authored contract sitting in the work directory comes back as the pipeline's object. This is the mechanism the row exists to observe, and a survival test that still passed here would be asserting that a file exists rather than that it is the one the verifier wrote

mutations.name: a-second-owner-may-claim-a-registered-name
mutations.anchor:
held = _OWNERS.setdefault(name, owner)
    if held != owner:
        raise NameConflict(
            f"{name!r} is registered to {held!r}; {owner!r} may not claim it too")
mutations.why: the last writer wins instead of the first owner holding, which is the state the work directory was already in -- four collisions found by their damage rather than by anything refusing them. A registry that records without refusing is a comment

mutations.name: a-writer-need-not-own-the-name-it-resolves
mutations.anchor:
held = _OWNERS.get(name)
    if held != owner:
        raise NameConflict(
            f"{owner!r} may not write {name!r}: it is registered to {held!r}")
    return Path(work_dir) / name
mutations.why: `path` degenerates into a join, so the runner's write is registered in appearance only: pointing it at any name, owned by anyone or by nobody, would succeed. The register-time refusal above cannot catch that, because a caller that never registers never reaches it
